The last two comments are inspecting the wrong code path. A full `deny` does remove matching tool definitions before the request is sent to the model in V1 `dev` / 1.18.19.

The relevant path is:

1. Request preparation calls [`resolveTools(input)`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts#L148) and returns that filtered record as `prepared.tools` ([lines 181–185](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts#L181-L185)).
2. [`resolveTools`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4/packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts#L208-L214) merges agent and session permissions, computes disabled tools, and filters them out.
3. [`Permission.disabled`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4/packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts#L204-L214) treats the effective final matching rule as tool-disabling when its argument pattern is `"*"` and its action is `"deny"`.

The `sessionPreapprovedTools` code cited above is inside the `GitLabWorkflowLanguageModel` integration. It controls workflow approval behavior and operates on the **already-filtered** `prepared.tools`; it is not the general LLM tool-list filter: [`llm.ts#L149-L153`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4/packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts#L149-L153).

I also ran this single-file Bun reproduction directly against commit `b155b15694dbcc6768f11d2f25cc2bdd1f738ab4` (`packages/opencode` version 1.18.19). It calls the real `LLMRequestPrep.prepare`, rather than copying the filtering logic:

We're seeing this bug with MCP remote server headers, with an additional twist: the env var **is set** in `process.env`, yet `{env:...}` still resolves to empty at runtime.

**Setup:**
- opencode 1.18.18 on Linux
- 5 remote MCP servers with `"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MY_TOKEN}" }`
- A plugin injects tokens into `process.env` at init time (before config load)
- `opencode debug config` resolves `{env:MY_TOKEN}` correctly — shows `"Authorization": "Bearer <actual_token>"`
- The env var is confirmed present in `process.env`

**What happens:**
- All 5 MCP servers fail with 401 from the remote endpoint
- Server-side logs show `Authorization: Bearer` (empty — no token value)
- `{file:/path/to/token}` works perfectly as a workaround — same setup, just `{file:...}` instead of `{env:...}`

**Key observation:**
`opencode debug config` (separate CLI process) resolves `{env:...}` correctly, but the running opencode session's MCP transport gets the empty value. This suggests either:
1. The substitution runs at config load but the substituted headers aren't passed to the MCP transport's `requestInit`, or
2. The MCP transport re-reads the raw (unsubstituted) config, or
3. `process.env` isn't available at the point where the MCP transport resolves headers

The `{file:...}` path works because it reads from disk at substitution time, while `{env:...}` depends on `process.env` being available in the right context.

**Workaround:** Use `{file:/path/to/token}` instead of `{env:TOKEN}` — this works at runtime for MCP remote server headers.

Same failure on beta-17728, and it hits the TUI too: local plugin files break in the TUI client (`plugins/tui/` discovery and `cli.json` path entries) as well as server-side. A few data points that might help:

Additional repro material for the verification pass noted above.

**Scope, up front:** these were observed on **v1.18.18**, which does *not* contain #35272 — GitHub's compare API reports `v1.18.18...bf01264` as `diverged` rather than `behind`, i.e. that merge commit is not an ancestor of the tag, and `toSessionError` is absent from `packages/core/src` on both `dev` and `production`. So this is **not** evidence that the fix failed. It is extra repro surface for whoever runs the verification pass.

**The affected error family is wider than the single reported error.** The original report is `ModelUnavailableError`, but at least two siblings from `SessionRunnerModel` reach the same log-only path and produce byte-identical user-visible behaviour. Both were logged under the same `Failed to drain Session` message:

```
SessionRunnerModel.VariantUnavailableError: Variant unavailable for anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6: high
SessionRunnerModel.UnsupportedApiError: Unsupported API for amazon-bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6: aisdk:@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock
```

Both surface from model resolution during pre-stream setup — the mechanism described in the issue body — so all four members of `SessionRunnerModel.Error` (`ModelNotSelectedError`, `ModelUnavailableError`, `VariantUnavailableError`, `UnsupportedApiError`) plausibly share the same fate.

**Wire-level behaviour, identical for each:**

- `POST /api/session/{id}/prompt` returns `200` with a monotonic `admittedSeq`
- the session event log gains one `user` record and two `model-switched` records
- zero assistant output, and no error event of any kind
- the session goes idle shortly after `prompted`

Observed from an HTTP API consumer with no TUI attached, so no client-side rendering is involved — the durable event genuinely isn't there.

**Suggested addition to the verification pass:** exercise at least one non-`ModelUnavailableError` member of the family. A pass that only covers `ModelUnavailableError` could go green while `VariantUnavailableError` and `UnsupportedApiError` still fail silently, since the variant lookup and the API-support check sit at different points in resolution.

For reference, on `dev`/`production` the drain failure is still log-only in `packages/core/src/session/execution/local.ts` (`Effect.logError("Failed to drain Session", cause)`), with no conversion into a durable event, consistent with the issue's diagnosis.

The scoping choice here is the part I keep turning over. Out of scope says cloud relay, and the approval page is LAN/Tailscale only. That covers being in the next room, which is real and probably the common case. But the runs that actually sat stalled on me were the ones where I was on cellular and nowhere near that network, which is the same situation the problem statement opens with. If Tailscale is the intended answer for that, it might be worth saying so in the issue, since standing up a tailnet is a pretty different ask than scanning a QR code.

The other thing I'd think about early is what the approval page actually shows. Deciding on a bash command or an edit means having the command or the diff in front of you, and getting that onto a phone screen without it turning into a blind yes seems like what decides whether people read it or just tap approve on everything.

And related to the #43493 thread that got linked here: worth settling whether every pending prompt notifies. In a session that asks a lot, per-prompt pushes get muted fast, and then you're back to the stall with an extra step in front of it.

Follow-up investigation (verified with a real browser via Chrome DevTools MCP):

**The blank page is NOT about browser profiles or "fresh context" by itself.** The root cause is a split between two state layers:

1. **Session content / messages are server-side (DB)** — they display in any browser/profile/access as long as the URL is correct. Confirmed: a private tab and a fresh (incognito-style) browser profile could both display the session normally.

2. **The home/project sidebar list is client-side localStorage**, persisted per *server identity* (the base64 server URL in the route), in `packages/app/src/context/server.tsx` (`projects: Record<string, StoredProject[]>` persisted under `Persist.global("server", ["server.v3"])`, consumed by `home.project.forServer(conn)`).

Because the same backend is exposed under multiple URLs (`localhost` and a Tailscale hostname), each URL becomes a separate server identity in the Web UI:

- Projects added under one URL do **not** appear under another (each is a separate localStorage entry).
- Re-adding a project on the same URL makes it appear (it was already the same localStorage scope).
- A brand-new browser profile has empty localStorage, so the project list is empty until projects are (re-)added — but the session itself still loads, since sessions come from the server DB.

This also explains the "projects disappear / not synced" reports: the sidebar is filtering by which server identity the current browser connection is bound to.

**Suggested fix direction:** key the home project list by a server-side identifier (e.g., projectID or the canonical worktree path) instead of the URL-derived server key, or merge project lists for connections pointing at the same backend, so the sidebar is consistent regardless of which URL (localhost vs tailnet hostname) is used to reach the same server.

I ran into this on Kubuntu 24.04 using X11 while in Konsole. What I want to add is that the error you're trying to show already exists and is getting thrown away.

The reason turned out to be simple. I had no clipboard program installed at all. No xclip, no xsel, no wl-copy. Nothing told me that.

Here's what the code does. In packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts, copyCommand looks for wl-copy, xclip and xsel. If it finds none of them it returns nothing. getCopyMethod then falls back to clipboardy. All three of those paths end in .catch(() => undefined), so the error disappears.

Here's the part that matters. clipboardy doesn't fail quietly. Its linux backend throws this exact message.

"Couldn't find the xsel binary and fallback didn't work. On Debian/Ubuntu you can install xsel with: sudo apt install xsel. The bundled xsel fallback was not found. This can happen when running in a bundled environment (e.g. Node.js SEA)."

clipboardy ships its own copy of xsel and checks whether that file is really there, because in a bundled build it isn't. opencode is a single Bun binary and that file isn't in the installed package, so the second line is the one you hit here.

So the fix is smaller than writing a new error message. Show clipboardy's message instead of a generic failure. It already tells the user what to install.

One catch. That message says to install xsel, but image paste only uses xclip. read() runs xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o for it. So someone who installs xsel gets text copy working and image paste still broken. Pointing people at xclip fixes both. The troubleshooting page has the same problem. It lists apt install -y xclip # or apt install -y xsel as if either one works.

Something this fix won't reach. Once xclip is installed, copy stops failing and starts hanging instead. xclip has to stay alive to own the X selection, and the background process it forks holds the stdout pipe open, so command() never sees close and write() never settles. I had one sit pending for over eight minutes on a copy that actually worked. A pending promise never rejects, so surfacing errors doesn't help there. I'm filing that separately.

Two smaller things. writeOsc52 sends the escape through process.stdout.write, which is buffered and can get mixed in with the TUI drawing instead of reaching the terminal.
